title: Weyl's Polarization in Classical Invariant Theory: A Primer, with Worked Examples
summary: Hermann Weyl's The Classical Groups is a landmark work connecting classical invariant theory with modern representation theory. It shows how polynomial invariants of the general linear, orthogonal, and symplectic groups can be systematically understood through linear representations and tensor methods. The current note is primarily based on a personal reading of the book of Weyl and of the more accessible books Classical Invariant Theory by Kraft and Procesi and by Olver.
